sentences.text: Author: Ashutosh Kumar Bench: Ashutosh Kumar

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR  S.B. Criminal Misc. Application for Suspension of Sentence  No.20/2023  In  S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 86/2023 Gyan Chand S/o Sh. Chiranji Lal, age 72 years, R/o Indira Colony,
Tonk, P.S. Kotwali, District Tonk, Seller and Owner of Firm Gendi Lal Chiranji Lal Jain Kirana Merchant.
At present confined in Tonk Jail  ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan through PP  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Atul Kumar Jain For Respondent(s) : Mr. Suresh Kumar, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHUTOSH KUMAR  Order 31/01/2023

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties on the application filed for suspension of sentence and perused the entire material available on record.

Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that there is no reliable and legally acceptable evidence to hold accused- applicant guilty for the alleged offence(s) and there is every likelihood of succeeding in the criminal revision petition.
Learned counsel further submits that final hearing of the petition is likely to take time thus sentence of the accused-applicant may be suspended.
Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the prayer regarding suspension of sentence.
(2 of 2) [SOSR-20/2023] I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner was convicted and sentenced for the offence under Section 7(1)/16 of the Gyan Chand S/O Sh. Chiranji Lal vs State Of Rajasthan on 31 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142369074/
1 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act in regular criminal case No.04/2003 by the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tonk.

entities.text: Gyan Chand S/O Sh. Chiranji Lal vs State Of Rajasthan on 31 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner preferred regular appeal which was dismissed by the Court of Sessions Judge, Tonk as Criminal Appeal CIS No.133/2016 vide judgment dated 12.01.2023 by which the learned Appellate Court has upheld the judgment and sentence passed by the learned trial Court.
Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that accused-applicant was on bail during trial as well as during pendency of appeal and presently he is behind the bars.
Without commenting upon the merits of the case, I deem it just and proper to suspend the sentence awarded to the applicant.

Accordingly, the application for suspension of sentence is allowed and it is ordered that the sentence awarded by the learned trial Court and affirmed by the learned appellate Court against the accused-applicant namely, Gyan Chand S/o Shri Chiranji Lal in the matter shall remain suspended during pendency of petition and he shall be released on bail, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- along with two sureties in the sum of Rs.50,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with the stipulation that he shall appear before this court on 28th February, 2023 and thereafter as and when called upon to do so.

(ASHUTOSH KUMAR),J AARZOO ARORA /31 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
